newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ALPINE SKIING-WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS WEIGH ON AUSTRIANS' MINDS.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS WEIGH ON AUSTRIANS' MINDS.

text.p: Hans Knauss and his Austrian team mates will have next weeks world championships on their minds when they race in a World Cup super-G on Wednesday.

Ten Austrians are competing for just four super-G team places at the Alpine skiing championships in Sestriere, Italy, and national coaches will be looking closely at Wednesdays results before picking the squad.
Knauss won the season's only previous men's super-G, in Val d'Isere in December, when four of the top five finishers were Austrians.

The men's super-G will be the first event of the two-week championships next Monday and racers in Laax will be trying to strike a fine balance between doing their best in the last speed event before Sestriere and not taking any undue risks.
After two hard weekends in Wengen and Kitzbuehel, with three downhills, two slaloms and a combined event, many of the skiers were feeling the strain.

The last week has been very trying with practices and races in Wengen and Kitzbuehel. Those races leave their mark on you, said Switzerland's William Besse, who finished third in the first Kitzbuehel downhill, a sprint event over two legs.
I want to recharge before the championships, added Besse. Right now Im just tired."

Wednesday's race should provide a guide to who to watch next Monday. No clear favourite has emerged in super-G in recent years, though Norway's Atle Skaardal holds both the World Cup and world championship titles. Last season's six super-G races produced six different winners.

Downhill specialists Luc Alphand of France and Italys Kristian Ghedina, who both have their eyes on the overall World Cup, may fancy their chances in Laax, which is hosting a super-G for the first time since 1989.
Neither has yet won a super-G though Alphand came close with two second places last season.

With four more super-G events to race after the world championships, Alphand and Ghedina could mount a strong challenge for the overall cup if they could only translate their success in the downhill into wins in the sport's newest discipline.
Norway's Kjetil Andre Aamodt, the super-G gold medallist at the 1992 Olympics and a bronze medallist in Lillehammer, will also want to underline his superb form as he heads for Sestriere.
Aamodt, the 1994 overall champion, tops the current rankings with 701 points, closely pursued by Alphand with 637 and Ghedina with 620.
